original_value: Earth Observation Data Cubes (EODC) have emerged as a promising solution to efficiently and effectively handle Big Earth Observation (EO) Data generated by satellites and made freely and openly available from different data repositories. The aim of this Special Issue, “Earth Observation Data Cube”, in Data, is to present the latest advances in EODC development and implementation, including innovative approaches for the exploitation of satellite EO data using multi-dimensional (e.g., spatial, temporal, spectral) approaches. This Special Issue contains 14 articles covering a wide range of topics such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), Analysis Ready Data (ARD), interoperability, thematic applications (e.g., land cover, snow cover mapping), capacity development, semantics, processing techniques, as well as national implementations and best practices. These papers made significant contributions to the advancement of a more Open and Reproducible Earth Observation Science, reducing the gap between users’ expectations for decision-ready products and current Big Data analytical capabilities, and ultimately unlocking the information power of EO data by transforming them into actionable knowledge.

result.paraphrase: Earth Observation Data Cubes (EODC) have become a promising way to manage Big Earth Observation (EO) data efficiently and effectively, using satellite-generated datasets that are freely and openly accessible from various repositories. This Special Issue, “Earth Observation Data Cube” in Data, aims to showcase the newest advances in EODC development and implementation, including innovative methods for exploiting satellite EO data through multi-dimensional approaches such as spatial, temporal, and spectral analysis. It includes 14 articles spanning topics such as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), Analysis Ready Data (ARD), interoperability, thematic applications like land cover and snow cover mapping, capacity building, semantics, processing techniques, and national implementations and best practices. Collectively, these papers have made substantial contributions to more open and reproducible Earth Observation science, narrowing the gap between user demands for decision-ready products and current Big Data analytics capabilities, and ultimately unlocking the informational value of EO data by turning it into actionable knowledge.
